hints: Find the driving force exerted by the cyclist using $P = F_D \times v$ with $P = 180\text{ W}$ and $v = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the component of the weight acting down the slope: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\alpha = 70 \times 10 \times 0.05$.
Apply Newton's second law up the slope: $F_D - F - mg\sin\alpha = ma$, where $m = 70\text{ kg}$ and $a = -0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$, then solve for $F$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the driving force $F_D$ at speed $v = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $P = F_D \times v$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{180}{6} = 30\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law in the direction of motion up the inclined plane:
$$F_D - F - mg\sin\alpha = ma$$
$$30 - F - 70(10)(0.05) = 70(-0.2)$$
$$30 - F - 35 = -14$$

Solve for the resistance force $F$:
$$-5 - F = -14 \implies F = 14 - 5 = 9\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Newton's Second Law: Finds driving force $180/6 = 30\text{ N}$, writes $30 - F - 70(10)(0.05) = 70(-0.2)$, and solves to get $F = 9\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Determine the forward driving force $F_D$ produced by the cyclist from the power formula:
$$P = F_D \times v$$
Substitute $P = 180\text{ W}$ and $v = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$180 = F_D \times 6$$
Divide both sides by $6$:
$$F_D = \frac{180}{6} = 30\text{ N}$$

Identify all forces acting on the cyclist and bicycle parallel to the inclined plane:
- Forward driving force: $F_D = 30\text{ N}$
- Constant resistance force: $F$ (directed down the hill, opposing motion)
- Downward component of total weight: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\alpha = (70)(10)(0.05) = 35\text{ N}$

Apply Newton's second law along the slope in the uphill direction:
$$\sum F_{\text{up}} = ma$$
$$F_D - F - mg\sin\alpha = ma$$
Substitute $m = 70\text{ kg}$ and acceleration $a = -0.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$30 - F - 35 = 70(-0.2)$$

Simplify and solve the linear equation for $F$:
$$-5 - F = -14$$
Add $5$ to both sides:
$$-F = -14 + 5 = -9$$
Multiply both sides by $-1$:
$$F = 9\text{ N}$$
Thus, the magnitude of the resistance force is $F = 9\text{ N}$.

hints: At a steady speed, acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), so the driving force equals the sum of resistance and the component of weight.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law with zero acceleration ($a = 0$) up the hill:
$$\frac{P}{v} - F - mg\sin\alpha = 0$$
$$\frac{180}{v} - 9 - 35 = 0$$
$$\frac{180}{v} = 44$$

Solve for the steady speed $v$:
$$v = \frac{180}{44} = \frac{45}{11} \approx 4.09\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Newton's Second Law: Sets up $180/v - 9 - 35 = 0$ and obtains $v = 4.09\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (or $45/11\text{ m s}^{-1}$).

teacher_walkthrough:
State the condition for a steady speed: acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), which means the resultant force along the slope is zero:
$$\sum F = 0$$
$$F_D - F - mg\sin\alpha = 0$$

Express the driving force in terms of power and speed:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{180}{v}$$

Substitute the known values ($F = 9\text{ N}$ from part (a) and $mg\sin\alpha = 70(10)(0.05) = 35\text{ N}$):
$$\frac{180}{v} - 9 - 35 = 0$$
$$\frac{180}{v} - 44 = 0$$
$$\frac{180}{v} = 44$$

Multiply both sides by $v$ and divide by $44$:
$$44v = 180$$
$$v = \frac{180}{44} = \frac{45}{11}\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Compute the decimal value:
$$v = 4.0909\ldots \approx 4.09\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus, the steady speed the cyclist can maintain is $4.09\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
